html:
SMTO-ART-0029 — SMTO couldn't match a background command's result to its Task

GUID: 79006767-69d0-4fbb-8671-64dbf0952950
Slug: artifact-job-ownership-invalid
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • A command running in the background sent back a result SMTO couldn't match to the Task that started it, so SMTO didn't record it. The command may still have done its work, and related files are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task and find the step that started the background command. Note whether it shows as still running, finished, or Outcome unknown. SMTO couldn't record the command's result, so the step's status is the best sign of how far it got.
  2. On the computer where the command ran, check whether its work already happened, for example whether the expected file exists or the service was restarted. The command may have finished even though SMTO couldn't link its result to this Task.
  3. Only if the work didn't happen, ask SMTO in the conversation to run the command again. Starting it a second time while the first result is unclear could make the same change twice.
  4. Don't delete this Task's files or its conversation while this is being sorted out. Those files show what the command produced and are needed to work out which Task it belongs to.

What success looks like

  • The step shows a finished result, and later background commands in this Task report their results without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which command was running and on which Gateway. Don't start the same command again until you know whether the first one finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A job record or its terminal/initial receipt failed ownership checks: the job belongs to a different run, the receipt's job_id or operation_id does not match the job, or a Gateway job record is not a valid object.

What this means

  • Job protection cannot parse a job record as an object, or job publication/settlement detects a different owner, mismatched job/result ID or inconsistent launch receipt. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Job protection cannot parse a job record as an object, or job publication/settlement detects a different owner, mismatched job/result ID or inconsistent launch receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact job owner, run and correlated original/result identities before altering retention or state.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the job in native_jobs and its receipts in native_artifacts (MemoryRunStore._put_job and settle_job), and on the Gateway the job records that ArtifactMaintenance._protected_runs reads, to find which run owns the job_id and why the receipt identity differs. Keep the affected artifacts until ownership is established, and do not re-dispatch the job while its earlier outcome is unresolved.
  • Inspect and reconcile the job's exact ownership and receipt identities; preserve artifacts until that ownership is established.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported reconciliation establishes coherent job ownership and preserves protected artifact evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
